items.summary: Kookmin University established the QNX Centre Korea on Nov. 4 in partnership with QNX, a global provider of embedded software and operating systems, to provide specialized education in the field. The university said the center will serve as a platform for industry-academia collaboration aimed at nurturing talent in embedded software. Through the partnership, Kookmin University becomes the first university in Korea to introduce a curriculum based on QNX technology. QNX, a division of BlackBerry Limited, provides operating systems and software development technologies for industries where safety and reliability are critical, including the automotive, medical device and industrial automation sectors. The university plans to develop the center into a hub for embedded software education and industry-academia cooperation, connecting academic institutions, government agencies and industry partners across Korea. The initiative aims to cultivate skilled professionals in various fields, including software-defined vehicles, robotics, industrial automation, smart factories and the industrial internet

He added that the university would support students in taking part in key national research projects and preparing to lead future industries. items.title: Education minister resigns amid backlash over CSAT anti-cheating measures
items.title_zh: 因高考防作弊措施引发强烈不满，韩国教育部长辞职
items.summary: Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin offered to resign on Sunday, taking responsibility for confusion over anti-cheating measures in the run-up to the 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test (CSAT). President Lee Jae Myung immediately accepted his resignation. "Last-minute changes in preparations for the CSAT caused inconvenience to the public, particularly test takers," Choi said in a statement released by the ministry. While the exam now over, Choi acknowledged responsibility for the confusion and announced his decision to resign. The resignation followed mounting criticism of the ministry's belated response to concerns over artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted cheating ahead of the CSAT, Korea's high-stakes college entrance exam. The government repeatedly revised its anti-cheating measures just days before the test, leaving students and test administrators scrambling to keep up with the changes. Ha Jin-yong, a professor in the university’s Department of AI Convergence Electronics Engineering, launched the company in 2019. It specializes in medical imaging devices for cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diagnosis. The investors included participation from InterVest, Life Asset Management, Ryukyung PSG Asset Management, Hyundai Venture Investment, L&S Venture Capital, Eugene Investment & Securities and EcoPro Partners. Investors recognized Raywatt’s achievements in commercializing its technology both in Korea and overseas. The company’s technology has been used in more than 100 clinical cases at Severance Cardiovascular Hospital in Seoul. It has also been designated an innovative prototype product by the Public Procurement Service. items.summary: The Coast Guard said Sunday it has located an object believed to be a sunken vessel on the seabed near where a fishing boat went missing off South Korea's west coast last week. The unidentified object was detected by naval sonar at 7:55 p.m. Saturday, according to the Taean Coast Guard. The object lies 52 meters deep and roughly 41 kilometers northwest of an island off Taean, about 110 km southwest of Seoul. The location is near the site where the fishing boat Haegwangho went missing Wednesday. Officials said they are working to determine whether the object is linked to the vessel. The search entered its fifth day Sunday for the seven crew members who remain missing, as well as the 7.93-ton boat. High waves and strong winds have hampered search and rescue operations. The Navy said it is sending its 3,500-ton Tongyeong rescue and salvage ship to the site to carry out a detailed underwater search. items.title: Seoul district prepares to bring pet funerals directly to residents' doors

items.summary: Courier scooters in Seoul deliver everything from midnight kimchi stew to designer handbags in under an hour, and soon grieving pet owners in the city's east will be able to summon a hearse just as easily. Starting in December, Seongdong District, located just east of downtown Seoul, will roll out a municipal mobile pet funeral service, dispatching specialized vans to residents' homes to collect deceased pets, hold a memorial ceremony and perform odorless, smoke-free cremations before returning the ashes in an urn. The initiative, finalized through a partnership signed earlier this month between the district office and local pet funeral operator Petmoon, tackles a thorny urban dilemma in Korea’s densely packed capital. While roughly 1 in 4 Korean households — an estimated 15 million people nationwide — now lives with a companion animal, strict zoning rules have pushed licensed pet crematoriums to the suburban fringes. items.title: Why are young Koreans falling for Japanese animated series 'Chiikawa?'
items.title_zh: 为什么年轻的韩国人会迷上日本动画片《奇可万岁！》？
items.summary: "I'm worried everything will sell out. They'll keep restocking, right?" A long line of customers stretched outside the Chiikawa Shop on the third floor of I'Park Mall in Yongsan District, Seoul, Nov. 5. A quick count put the number of people waiting at well over 50. They had come to buy merchandise featuring characters from the Japanese animated series "Chiikawa." One shopper, surnamed Kim, 27, emerged carrying a large bag filled with stuffed toys, figurines and key rings. "I came to love the animation because I find hope in the way Chiikawa overcomes life's hardships and grows along the way," Kim said with a laugh. "I kept adding things to my basket and ended up spending 460,000 won ($315)." "Chiikawa," created by Japanese manga artist Nagano, depicts the everyday lives of characters collectively described as "something small and cute." In Korea, the series has gained a large following not only among children but also among people in their 20s and 30s. items.summary: RIYADH — The Transport General Authority (TGA) said that delivery orders in Saudi Arabia exceeded 129 million in the third quarter of 2026, marking a 25.2 percent increase compared to the same period in 2025. The growth reflects rising demand for delivery services and increased reliance on delivery applications across the Kingdom.According to the authority’s quarterly statistical bulletin, Riyadh accounted for the largest share of delivery orders at 44 percent, followed by Makkah region 22 percent, Eastern Province 16percent, Madinah region 5 percent , and Asir region4 percent. Qassim accounted for 3 percent of total requests, while Tabuk and Hail each recorded 2 percent. Al-Jouf, Northern Borders, Jazan, and Najran each accounted for one percent while Al-Baha recorded 0.28 percent.The authority reaffirmed its commitment to developing the delivery sector, enhancing operational efficiency, and improving service quality. These efforts aim to support the sector’s growth and sustainability and strengthen the reliability of delivery services across the Kingdom.

items.title: Saudi Arabia calls for mutual guarantees for lasting regional security at Mediterranean Dialogues
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯在地中海对话上呼吁为持久的地区安全提供相互保障
items.summary: NAPLES — Advisor and Special Envoy of the Minister of Foreign Affairs for Negotiations and Peace Efforts Manal Radwan affirmed that Saudi Arabia remains steadfast in pursuing a balanced strategy that combines containment, deterrence, and dialogue to safeguard regional peace and stability. She emphasized that the Kingdom’s unwavering commitment to defending its national security, preserving the security and stability of the Gulf, and protecting the vital waterways of the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab Strait extends far beyond the region, serving the interests of the entire world. Radwan made the remarks while addressing a session titled "Redefining Security: Iran, the Straits, and the Future of the Regional Order" at the Mediterranean Dialogues (MED) conference in Naples, Italy. She called for a sustainable regional security architecture in which each state's security is linked to that of its neighbors and not achieved at another's expense, founded on mutual security guarantees, so that the end of one round of conflict does not merely set the stage for a more violent one. “Temporary arrangements will not work unless they are aligned with long-term strategic frameworks. Dealing with armed groups outside state control requires a political vision, not only a security one, that addresses the local causes of their emergence and their links to the external parties that support and exploit them,” she said.Radwan said Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) member states are united in their objectives and that their roles should complement one another in supporting mediation, de-escalation, and the prevention of a new war, paving the way for confidence-building. “Regional dialogue and international stability are closely linked, and there is no place in the region for any hegemonic power,” she emphasized.On Yemen, Radwan said the war is at its core an intra-Yemeni conflict, and the Kingdom supports a resolution through political and economic tracks in line with the UN-led roadmap. She warned that merely managing the region's crises for years to come without addressing their root causes could have catastrophic consequences for all. Manal called for collective action to seize the current opportunity for a comprehensive and sustainable solution that serves all parties, and that includes the realization of a Palestinian state, fosters regional integration, and keeps pace with global geostrategic shifts.

items.title: Saudi Arabia deports 11,915 illegal residents in a week
items.title_zh: 沙特阿拉伯在一周内驱逐了11915名非法居留者
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi security authorities arrested a total of 10,783 illegal residents in a week. The arrests were made in the joint inspections, carried out by the security forces in collaboration with the relevant government agencies, during the period between November 12 and 18, the Ministry of Interior announced on Saturday. Those who were arrested include 5,718 violators of the Residency Law, 2,797 violators of the Border Security Law, and 2,268 violators of the Labor Law. A total of 11,915 illegal residents were deported while 23,250 violators were referred to their diplomatic missions to obtain travel documents and 10,814 violators were referred to complete their travel reservations. The total number of people who were arrested while trying to cross the border into the Kingdom accounted for 1,373. A total of 28 people were arrested while attempting to leave the Kingdom illegally. Some 14 people involved in giving transportation, shelter, and employment for violators were also arrested. A total of 40,941 expatriates, including 38,730 men and 2,211 women, are currently undergoing procedures to enforce legal measures for violations. The Ministry of Interior has warned that any person, who facilitates the illegal entry of individuals into the Kingdom, transports them on its territory, provides them with shelter or any other assistance or service, will be penalized with up to 15 years in prison and a fine of up to SR1 million, and that the vehicles used for transportation or houses used for giving shelter will be confiscated. The ministry urged the public to report any cases of violation by calling the number 911 in the regions of Makkah, Riyadh, and the Eastern Province and the numbers 999 and 996 in the rest of the Kingdom’s regions.

items.title: Foreign investors inject SR786 million into 131 Saudi-listed companies
items.title_zh: 外国投资者向131家沙特上市公司注入7.86亿里亚尔
items.summary: RIYADH — Foreign investors purchased a total of 34.9 million shares, valued at approximately SR786 million, on the Saudi Stock Exchange (Tadawul). According to a report on changes in foreign ownership, covering the trading week ended November 19, their holdings increased in 131 companies listed on Tadawul. Meanwhile, foreign investors reduced their holdings in 197 other companies by selling 53.3 million shares worth approximately SR929 million. Their ownership remained unchanged in 71 other companies. The Saudi stock market’s main index, Tadawul, ended the week down 167.6 points, or 1.6 percent, from the previous week, closing at 10,158.9 points. Meanwhile, the parallel market index, Nomu, declined by 337.72 points, or 1.5 percent, over the same period, closing at 21,716.4 points.

items.title: Saudi air defenses intercept 3 Houthi missiles fired toward Riyadh
items.title_zh: 沙特防空部队拦截了3枚朝利雅得发射的胡塞导弹
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi air defenses intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles launched by the terrorist Houthi militia toward Riyadh. This was disclosed by Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki, spokesperson of the Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen. He said that two drones, fired by Houthi militia toward the southern region, were intercepted and destroyed.

items.title: Coalition launches major military operation to neutralize Houthi threats against Saudi Arabia
items.title_zh: 联军发起大规模军事行动，以消除胡塞武装对沙特阿拉伯的威胁
items.summary: RIYADH — The Joint Forces Command of the Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen launched on Friday a military operation to neutralize sources of threat used by the Houthi terrorist militia to target civilians in Saudi Arabia and Yemen, including vital facilities supporting its military activities.The coalition said the operation targeted Houthi military capabilities and infrastructure involved in weapons smuggling and transportation, adding that operations were continuing against military targets in the governorates of Sanaa, Saada and Taiz.The coalition announced the destruction of seven legitimate military targets that had been designated for military use and supporting the Houthis’ military activities.It also confirmed the destruction of six workshops used by the militia to support its military capabilities.The coalition said its operations in Sanaa focused on destroying and neutralizing sources of threat to prevent attacks against civilians in Saudi Arabia and Yemen.It also announced the neutralization of one of the Houthi terrorist militia’s main supply facilities in Sanaa.The Joint Forces Command had earlier called on civilians to evacuate the port of Hodeidah in accordance with an accompanying map to ensure their safety.

items.title: ZATCA foils six attempts to smuggle over 2.3 million amphetamine pills through Duba Port
items.title_zh: ZATCA挫败六起企图通过杜巴港走私230多万粒安非他明药片的行动
items.summary: RIYADH — Saudi customs authorities at Duba Port have foiled six attempts to smuggle more than 2.3 million amphetamine pills concealed in shipments arriving in the Kingdom through the port.Hamoud Al-Harbi, spokesperson for the Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA), said six trucks arrived in the Kingdom through Duba Port carrying shipments of concrete bricks.The narcotics were discovered concealed inside the hollow cavities of the bricks during customs inspections using advanced security technologies and detection dogs.Al-Harbi said that following the seizures, the authority coordinated with the General Directorate of Narcotics Control (GDNC) to apprehend the intended recipient of the narcotics inside the Kingdom, resulting in his arrest.He reaffirmed ZATCA's commitment to tightening customs controls over the Kingdom's imports and exports across all customs ports and combating smuggling attempts.Al-Harbi emphasized that these efforts are in line with one of the authority's key strategic objectives of enhancing security and protecting society by preventing the smuggling of narcotics and other prohibited substances.He added that the authority continues to carry out its duties in close coordination and cooperation with its partners at the Ministry of Interior and the General Directorate of Narcotics Control.

items.title: Japan plans to offer Saudi Arabia 16 million barrels of additional oil storage, buy up to 8 million barrels
items.title_zh: 日本计划向沙特阿拉伯提供1600万桶额外石油储存，并购买多达800万桶石油
items.summary: RIYADH — Japan intends to provide Saudi Arabia with an additional 16 million barrels of crude oil storage capacity and purchase up to 8 million barrels of Saudi crude for its national reserves, Saudi Press Agency reported on Friday.The announcement came following a virtual meeting between Saudi Minister of Energy and Minister of Industry and Mineral Resources Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman and Japanese Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry Ryosei Akazawa on Nov. 9, 2026.During the meeting, the two ministers reaffirmed the strong and longstanding strategic partnership between Saudi Arabia and Japan and discussed ways to further strengthen bilateral cooperation, particularly in the energy sector.Following discussions within the joint task force established in May 2026, Saudi Arabia reaffirmed that it regards Japan as a strategic partner and attaches great importance to supporting its long-term energy security through stable and reliable crude oil supplies.Japan expressed its deep appreciation to Saudi Arabia for its continued provision of stable and reliable crude oil supplies.The Kingdom has already begun replenishing joint oil stockpiling tanks in Japan.Recognizing the longstanding importance of the Joint Crude Oil Stockpiling Project, established in 2010, and its recently demonstrated effectiveness, Japan intends to make an additional 16 million barrels of crude oil storage capacity available to Saudi Arabia for a limited period through its national stockpiling facilities.The additional capacity would bring the total storage capacity available to the Kingdom under the arrangement to 24 million barrels, including the existing capacity of 8 million barrels.Japan also intends to purchase up to 8 million barrels of Saudi crude oil for its national stockpile reserves, subject to favorable market conditions and the completion of necessary internal procedures.The two countries will also cooperate under Japan's "POWERR Asia" initiative to enhance energy security across Asia, building on the AZEC Ministerial Work Programme for Strengthening Oil Stockpiling presented at the ministerial meeting on Oct. 8.The program outlines future measures to develop institutional frameworks and infrastructure for oil stockpiling across Asia, strengthen cooperation with oil-producing countries and coordinate emergency responses.The two ministers welcomed the continued engagement between Saudi Arabia and Japan and expressed their shared aspiration to further strengthen their strategic energy partnership.Both ministries will continue discussions to explore additional opportunities for energy cooperation, enhance the existing joint crude oil stockpiling scheme and maximize its potential.

items.title: Saudi Arabia reserves legitimate right to defend its territory, people and national interests: Al-Khuraiji
items.title_zh: 库赖吉：沙特阿拉伯保留捍卫其领土、人民和国家利益的合法权利
items.summary: NAPLES — Saudi Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Waleed Al-Khuraiji reaffirmed that the Kingdom reserves its legitimate right to defend its territory, people and national interests in accordance with international law.His remarks came during a session titled "Securing Strategic Chokepoints and Rethinking Maritime Security" on Thursday, held on the sidelines of the Mediterranean Dialogues (MED) conference in Naples, Italy.Al-Khuraiji said recent developments in maritime corridors underscore the close interconnectedness between maritime security, regional stability and global prosperity.He noted that the security of strategic waterways, from the Red Sea and Bab Al-Mandab Strait to the Strait of Hormuz, is a matter of international concern.He emphasized that protecting strategic maritime corridors remains a fundamental priority that requires effective regional and international cooperation.The deputy minister stressed the importance of focusing on diplomatic efforts, de-escalation and addressing the root causes of regional instability to ensure that vital waterways remain safe and open in accordance with international law.On Yemen, Al-Khuraiji reaffirmed Saudi Arabia's continued commitment to achieving security and prosperity in the country.He also stressed the importance of confronting any attempts to use Yemeni territory to threaten neighboring countries or international navigation.
